exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Second Moment of a Random Variable

question.text:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{2}{5}, & x=1 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{5}, & x=2 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{5}, & x=3 \end{cases} \]

Calculate $\textrm E[X^2].$
question.explanation:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of $X^2$ is given by \[ \textrm E[X^2] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^2 \cdot f(x). \]

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

\begin{align} \textrm E[X^2] &= \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^2 \cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=1^2\cdot \dfrac{2}{5}+2^2\cdot \dfrac{1}{5}+3^2\cdot \dfrac{2}{5}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2}{5}+\dfrac{4}{5}+\dfrac{18}{5}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{24}{5}. \end{align}

question.text:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{3}{10}, & x=0 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{2}, & x=1 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{5}, & x=2 \end{cases} \]

Calculate $\textrm E[X^2].$
question.explanation:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of $X^2$ is given by \[ \textrm E[X^2] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^2 \cdot f(x). \]

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

\begin{align} \textrm E[X^2] &= \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^2 \cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=0^2\cdot \dfrac{3}{10}+1^2\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}+2^2\cdot \dfrac{1}{5}\\[5pt] &=0+\dfrac12+\dfrac45\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{13}{10}. \end{align}

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

\begin{align} \textrm E[X^2] &= \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^2 \cdot f(x)\\[5pt] &=0^2\cdot \dfrac{1}{10}+1^2\cdot \dfrac{1}{5}+2^2\cdot \dfrac 25+3^2\cdot 0+4^2\cdot \dfrac {1}{10}+5^2\cdot \dfrac 15+6^2\cdot 0\\[5pt] &=0\cdot \dfrac{1}{10}+1\cdot \dfrac{1}{5}+4\cdot \dfrac 25+9\cdot 0+16\cdot \dfrac {1}{10}+25\cdot \dfrac 15+36\cdot 0\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{42}{5}. \end{align}

Calculate $\textrm E[X^4].$
question.explanation:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of $X^4$ is given by \[ \textrm E[X^4] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^4 \cdot f(x). \]

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

example.title: Calculating Higher Moments of a Random Variable

question.text:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below. \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{5}{18}, & x =0 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{9}, & x=1 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{2}, & x=2 \end{cases} \]

Calculate $\textrm E[X^3].$
question.explanation:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of $X^3$ is given by \[ \textrm E[X^3] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^3 \cdot f(x). \]

Summing up the products of each cubed value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get \begin{align} \textrm E[X^3] & = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^3 \cdot f(x)\\[5pt] & = 0^3 \cdot \dfrac{5}{18} + 1^3 \cdot \dfrac{2}{9} + 2^3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\\[5pt] & = 0 \cdot \dfrac{5}{18} + 1 \cdot \dfrac{2}{9} + 8 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\\[5pt] & = 0 + \dfrac{2}{9} + 4\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{38}{9}. \end{align}

question.text: A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below. \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{2}, & x = 1 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{3}, & x = 2 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{6}, & x = 3 \end{cases} \] Calculate $\textrm E[X^3].$
question.explanation:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of $X^3$ is given by \[ \textrm E[X^3] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^3 \cdot f(x). \]

Summing up the products of each cubed value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get \begin{align} \textrm E[X^3] & = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^3 \cdot f(x)\\[5pt] & = 1^3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} + 2^3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{3} + 3^3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{6}\\[5pt] & = 1 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} + 8 \cdot \dfrac{1}{3} + 27 \cdot \dfrac{1}{6}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{9}{2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{23}{3}. \end{align}

question.text:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

$x$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$
$f(x)$ $0.4$ $0.5$ $0$ $0.1$

Calculate $\textrm E[X^4].$
question.explanation:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of $X^4$ is given by \[ \textrm E[X^4] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^4 \cdot f(x). \]

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get \begin{align} \textrm E[X^4] & = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^4 \cdot f(x)\\[5pt] & = 1^4 \cdot 0.4 + 2^4 \cdot 0.5 + 3^4 \cdot 0 + 4^4 \cdot 0.1 \\[5pt] & = 1 \cdot 0.4 + 16 \cdot 0.5 + 81 \cdot 0 + 256 \cdot 0.1 \\[5pt] & = 0.4 + 8 + 0 + 25.6\\[5pt] & = 34. \end{align}
